lines.text: [Verse 1 – Intimate baritone, conversational and dryly amused]
Life kept showing up beside me
With sawdust in her hair,
A busted map, a half-built dream,
And two good boots to spare.
She liked long roads and honest work,
Bad jokes and open skies—
Everything I said I wanted,
So I passed her fifty times.
I said she looked too complicated.
Probably way out of my league.
Besides, I’d learned that wanting more
Was just ambition dressed as greed.
**Pre-Chorus**
[Pre-Chorus – Drums enter, tension and anticipation rising]
I kept waiting to feel worthy.
She got tired of being polite.
Said, “You gonna keep on judging me,
Or finally swipe me right?”
**Chorus**
[Chorus – Full country-rock band, broad melody, joyful forward momentum]
So I swiped right on my life.
It said, “Where the hell you been?”
I said, “Waiting to feel worthy.”
It said, “Don’t start that shit again.”
Then it threw me in the shotgun seat,
Put the future into drive—
I spent years hoping someone chose me.
Then I swiped right on my life.
**Verse 2**
[Verse 2 – Rolling groove, playful swagger, crisp vocal phrasing]
Her profile said, “Some assembly.”
“Must provide your own damn tools.”
“No guarantees, no easy payments,
No protection against fools.”
“May include financial setbacks,
Heavy lifting, rain and doubt.”
“Applicant must quit pretending
Someone else will work it out.”
I read the terms and hesitated.
She said, “Son, you’ve seen the film.”
"You can keep researching the water,
Or jump in and learn to swim.”
**Pre-Chorus**
[Pre-Chorus – Stronger lift, Hammond organ building underneath]
I said, “What if I’m not ready?”
She said, “That line is getting old.
You’ve survived a hundred bad ideas.
Try one you actually chose.”
**Chorus**
[Chorus – Full band, wider and more confident]
So I swiped right on my life.
It said, “Where the hell you been?”
I said, “Waiting to feel worthy.”
It said, “Don’t start that shit again.”
Then it threw me in the shotgun seat,
Put the future into drive—
I spent years hoping someone chose me.
Then I swiped right on my life.
**Verse 3**
[Verse 3 – Open-road cinematic feel, emotionally warmer]
We had coffee in Arizona
With the whole horizon spread.
She asked what I was frightened of.
I named the living and the dead.
She listened like she’d heard it all,
Then grinned across the cup:
“That’s a fascinating history.
You still planning to get up?”
So I showed her what my hands could do.
She showed me what they’d missed.
Every door I called impossible
Had my fingerprints on it.
She wasn’t young or clean or easy.
Neither was I, truth be known.
But she looked better every mile
The farther we got from home.
**Bridge**
[Bridge – Half-time drop, dark electric guitar, vocal exposed and deliberate]
I’d been ghosted by tomorrow.
I’d been catfished by the past.
Courted every worst-case ending
Like the bastard had a chance.
Then I met myself outside that cage—
No filter, alibi or type.
Turns out I was what I’d been looking for.
Turns out I was my type.
**Final Chorus**
[Final Chorus – Huge live drums, soaring pedal steel and electric guitars, triumphant without sentimentality]
Yeah, I swiped right on my life.
It said, “Took your sweet-ass time.”
I said, “I brought some scars and baggage.”
It said, “Throw ’em in with mine.”
Now we’re making no damn promises
Except to show up and decide—
I spent years hoping someone chose me.
Then I swiped right on my life.
**Breakdown**
[Breakdown – Band drops back; baritone nearly alone]
No perfect match.
No master plan.
No guarantee it lasts.
Just this stubborn heart,
These working hands,
And no more dating my past.
**Final Refrain**
[Final Refrain – Full-band release, joyful, muscular and expansive]
I swiped right on my life—
And my life swiped right back.
Said, “Get your dreams unpacked, old man.
We’ve got some living to catch.”
Now every morning asks me
Who I’m willing to become.
I swiped right on my life—
And, goddamn...
We’re having fun.
**Spoken Outro**
[Spoken Outro – Instruments gradually recede; warm, amused, deeply grounded delivery]
She still leaves her clothes on the floor.
Spends money we don’t have.
Changes the destination halfway there.
But she’s mine.
And for the first time in my life—
So am I.
So am I.
